exclude: X-Ray trainer during startup. An instruction breakpoint at $CDB0 reached it before the five N replies led to the $084C hand-over.
Runtime workspace. VICE recorded no instruction fetches here in the sampled title and gameplay. The title temporarily holds the authored C800-CBFF tables at 0400-07FF before clearing that workspace.
HUD display cells and sprite pointers. $84FD regenerates the screen from $E158 and $E200 and $8329 installs the sprite pointers. The authored templates are tracked at their original addresses.

X-Ray bootstrap bytes observed intact in the crack intro before engine depacking. The $0816/$0819 loader copy wrote the identical 56-byte sequence from $96AA-$96E1. The Censor release has different RAM here and the loader call at $FFC0 enters KERNAL ROM.
5 parts: City, Forest, Prison ship and others
elsewhere: 5 parts: City, Forest, Prison ship and others

comments.text: Jump to the disk transition code at $0936. Engine callers pass the selection in A.
Clear the stage selection in $FF and the operand at $8001, then enter the initial load path at $0950.
Select VIC bank $0000 and screen $0400, set the background and border, hide sprites, and fill four screen pages with spaces.
Write ten prompt glyphs and their colours to the screen, then wait for a release and press on port 2 fire.
Loop through the rows of loading prompt text, mask each byte to a screen code, and write it to the displayed screen with its colour.
Copy 18 screen codes from $0919 to the line beginning at $05EB, with colour 1.
Copy 30 screen codes from $08FB into the screen at $0545 and set their foreground colour.
Ten characters selected by the prompt loop at $088D and placed at $063F.
Thirty bytes selected by the wide-message loop at $08E0.
Source of the 18 screen characters copied by $08CD.
Eleven screen codes used by the loop at $08BA.
Save A in $FF. Restore the KERNAL and input configuration. For a zero selection, draw the disk prompt and wait for fire before blacking out the display and selecting the file.
Restore the load-time chip and ROM configuration and blank the screen, then pass $FF plus six in A to $CC00.
Temporarily change CPU banking to $32 and copy sixteen pages beginning at $4000 to the RAM at $D000. The high bytes of the source and destination are patched once per page.
Patched high byte of the graphics copy source. It starts at $40 and advances after each full page.
High byte of the RAM destination under I/O. Incremented together with the source page, then the routine restores the previous processor port.
Reset VIC bank selection, disable sprites and silence SID gates and volume. Mask and clear CIA interrupts, restore KERNAL banking and vectors, and restore the CIA registers from $0A07 and $0A17.
Sixteen bytes written through the CIA 1 registers by $09F5-$0A04 before disk I/O.
Sixteen bytes written through the CIA 2 registers by $09F5-$0A04 before disk I/O.
Set VIC screen-enable bit 4 while clearing the high bit of the raster compare.
Clear VIC screen-enable bit 4 and the high bit of its raster compare.
Select bank $0000 and the display configuration for the loading screen, then move the loaded display and colour pages into their display addresses.
Sprite cells $40-$4F in VIC bank $4000, with 63 pixel bytes and one trailing byte in each slot. The sheet shows an upright figure, repeated horizontal bolts, crossed lines and small circular shapes.
Sprite cells $50-$5F. The first half shows humanoid animation and the latter cells show a sequence of large round silhouettes changing shape.
Sprite cells $60-$6F. These include triangular motion frames, narrow horizontal shapes, wide humanoid poses and a partial diagonal arc.
Sprite cells $70-$7F. The render begins with diagonal arcs, has low flat silhouettes in the middle, and ends with segmented mechanical figures.
Sprite cells $80-$8F. The sheet shows repeated slash arcs followed by separate round and low wide shapes.
Sprite cells $90-$9F. Small craft and assemblies occupy the left half, and the right half holds three progressively wider vehicle silhouettes.
Sprite cells $A0-$AF. There are several low vehicle outlines followed by humanoid poses and empty cells between sequences.
Sprite cells $B0-$BF. The sheet contains narrow frames with legs, circular details and two wide slash forms at the end.
Sprite cells $C0-$CF. Three diagonal shapes are followed by letter shapes for the game-over display and a sequence of upright figures.
Sprite cells $D0-$DF. Upright figures and left-facing horizontal shapes, with long narrow and curved shapes in the last cells.
Sprite cells $E0-$EF. A sequence of diagonals and expanding streaks appears before the narrow lightning silhouettes.
Sprite cells $F0-$F7. The artwork is mostly narrow fragmented vertical forms. Each 64-byte slot leaves its last byte outside the visible 24 by 21 pixels.
Sprite work page for playfield buffer 0. Its first two shapes have nonblank initial pixels. The byte writer at $860D can clear individual positions during the transition.
Destination of the unpatched sprite-copy instruction at $9CD9. In play $9CBD patches the high byte using the screen buffer and the selected sprite slot.
Sprite work page for playfield buffer 1. Its initial 256 bytes duplicate the page at $7E00. $8610 clears the same positions here when clearing the other page.
Clear the flag at $FFF8, bank in RAM beneath the ROMs, reset the stack and configure raster IRQ and sprite registers. Then build graphics lookup tables before dispatching on the stage selection.
Mutable operand of the instruction at $8000. Startup clears it at $0850. The stage transition code updates it for later loads.
Reverse the order of the four two-bit pixels in each nonzero input byte. Store the result in the lookup page at $FD00.
Clear the offset accumulator and blank the screen, then fill 128 low and high entries at $FE00 and $FE80 with successive multiples of $60.
Install the gameplay IRQ and NMI entry points. Set the initial packed-decimal timer to $004000, clear the scrolling screens, restore the status display and set the initial raster line.

Copy the screen-buffer selector to $90. Run the normal input, object, collision and status update calls, then wait on the raster handoff. Enter the alternate update at $8164 if $57 is set, or leave through $838B if $64 is set.
Ask $B6F4 for the mode value to put in $80. Clear the animation and screen selectors and reset entries $0522-$052B before using the alternate update loop.
Poll controls and call the alternate movement and encounter path. At the end of each pass toggle $90 and test the exit and encounter flags at $64 and $57.
Initialise the 24-entry per-object arrays at $0490, $04C0, $04D8, $0508 and $0598. Enable multicolour sprites and clear the stage-local counters and flags.
Start with an idle $FF latch, sample port 2, and refresh the latch when the divider at $65 expires. Use $27 to turn active-low fire into a fresh press pulse instead of repeating the same hold.
Set $10 to 1 and wait for its asynchronous clear before returning to the main loop.
Wait for the raster flag at $54 to become nonzero, then wait for it to fall again.
Update the scrolling origin through $991B when $80 is zero, then draw the visible tile window.
Update $4A with five times its previous value plus $D2 and $3D, using byte arithmetic. Return the updated byte in A.
For the first four stages, a negative value at $051C sets the transition reason to 2. The final stage also requires the sign bit of $D0 to be set.
Copy the loaded 1000 screen codes and four pages of colour bytes to the VIC screen and colour RAM. The last screen segment uses a 24-byte overlap so it ends at $07E7.
Copy two pages from $E158 and $E200 into the HUD screen at $EA58 and $EB00. Use each character index to look up its colour at $E800 before writing colour RAM.
Subtract one with borrow across the three packed decimal timer bytes in $89-$8B. Leaves decimal mode set for the caller to clear.
Decrement the decimal timer, clear decimal mode and OR the three bytes to detect zero. Set $64 to 1 when time runs out.
Fill both playfield screen buffers at $4000-$43FF and $4400-$47FF with zero.
Initialise the nine per-object flag entries written by the alternate update setup at $8181.
Drive the keyboard matrix with $7F and test column 7. If RUN/STOP is held low, wait for release. The X-Ray patch then allows a stage change unless the file letter is $4B.
Return to the stage tick after the matrix predicate decides against taking the transition.
Write the row mask from A to CIA 1 port A, read CIA 1 port B into X and return with its sign bit in the processor flags.
Poll port 2 fire between software countdown decrements. Return on active-low fire or when the three-level countdown expires.
Disable IRQs and copy the four pages at $C800-$CBFF to $0400-$07FF.
Copy the four pages at $0400-$07FF to $C800-$CBFF while clearing their original bytes.
Clear the player state and current animation bytes, then tail-call the player shape selection at $9E56.
Seed the byte index at $4A, then repeatedly derive an index through $837C, clear that position in the two sprite work pages at $7E00 and $7F00 and wait on the raster flag.
Run the playfield redraw and display handoff twice.
Update the playfield view, latch the joystick and tail-call $A11C.
Write $FF to CIA 1 port A and return its input state. The direction and fire lines are active low.
Dispatch to the music initialisation at $8AD7. A selects the track entry.
Dispatch to the sound reset path at $8BAD.
If the driver is disabled, clear the three SID voice controls. Otherwise update the tempo divider and the per-voice delay counters.
Read the next event from the pointer in $F0/$F1. $FE takes the reset path and $FF restarts the selected track. Other high-bit events select a handler through the pointer table at $9165.
While the indexed effect flag at $8FDC is nonzero, advance its playback counter. Load a pitch table pointer and set the indexed SID control and shared volume for normal effect steps.
Double the pitch number in A and load the low and high table bytes into the voice slots indexed by X at $8F2E and $8F31.

Save the track selector in $8F08. Copy the six default voice pointer bytes from $915F into the driver workspace and initialise the SID envelopes, tempo and waveform controls from the fixed defaults at $9143-$914C.
Enter the music pointer advance path with zero extra parameter bytes.
Add Y plus one to the current event pointer at $F0/$F1, propagating carry to the high byte.
Set $8F01 and copy the operand into both $8F00 and $8F02 before fetching the next event.
Set the indexed $8F19 flag and read its parameter into $8F1C for this voice.
Clear the indexed $8F19 flag and resume interpreting the stream.
Set the voice flag at $8F79 and write $0A to the selected attack-decay and sustain-release registers.
Clear the voice flag at $8F79 and resume at the next event.
Select control byte $42 for this voice.
Select control byte $50 for this voice.
Select the pulse waveform without gating it on in the stored control byte.
Select the triangle waveform without setting the gate bit in the stored control byte.
Clear the stored waveform control for this voice.
Clear $8F76 and set $8F73, then read the next parameters through the branch shared with $8C88.
Set $8F76 instead of $8F73, then join the parameter-reading path at $8C5D.
Enable the flag at $8FB2 and consume two parameters into $8FA2 and $8FA3.
Clear $8FB2 and advance to the next event.
Clear both $8F73 and $8F76, then advance the stream pointer.
Read a value into $8F8D and arm $8FC1, clear $8F49, then store the next parameter at $8FC4.
Clear both $8FC1 and $8FC4 for the indexed voice.
Select the branch controlled by $8F49, disable $8FC1, and update the paired values at $8F5E/$8F61 and $8F4F/$8F52 from the stream.
Reset the indexed enable at $8F49 and step to the next music event.
Read register offsets and values from the stream, write them relative to $D400 and stop on offset $AF.
Read the repeat count into $8FD0 and save the address of the next event in $8FCA/$8FCD.
Decrement $8FD0. If the count stays nonzero, replace the stream pointer with the address saved by command $9E.
Consume two stream bytes into the indexed fields at $8F90 and $8F93.
Read the tempo reload value into $FF and store a second parameter under the current track index at $8F0E.
Set the indexed effect flag at $8FDC, read later by $8858.
Clear the indexed effect flag at $8FDC.
Advance past the command and set the indexed flag at $8FD3.
Advance past the command and clear the indexed flag at $8FD3.
Read the count, pattern parameter and pattern pointer from the stream. Save the caller's stream pointer for the matching $94 command.
Decrement the pattern repeat count at $8F1F. While nonzero, jump to the saved pattern start. The zero case restores the caller's stream position.
Copy one operand into $8F96 and $8F97, load the next into $8F98 and enable the flags at $8F9F and $8F99.
Clear $8F99 and update SID filter routing at $D417 using the voice mask at $8FF7.
Set the indexed voice option at $8F84 and advance to the next event.
Clear the indexed option at $8F84 before fetching the next event.
Enable $8F40, copy the first operand into both $8F58 and $8F5B, and the second into $8F46.
Clear $8F40, then advance the pointer for the next event.
Set the indexed auxiliary field at $8FA9.
Clear the indexed auxiliary field at $8FA9.
Use the low three command bits to choose an envelope preset, fetch the two table values and write the selected voice's SID attack-decay and sustain-release registers.
Clear $8FDF, select control value $40 and initialise the indexed voice's two SID envelope bytes to 9 and 7.
Set the indexed flag at $8F3D and resume parsing.
Clear the indexed flag at $8F3D and resume parsing.
Per-voice field that receives the lookup result at $8EA3 when the command selects a preset.
Stored bytes immediately before the pair of options populated by command $B4.
First target of the value operand of command $B4.
Flag raised by command $B4 when it updates both options.
Second target of the parameter broadcast by command $B4.
The sign bit enables music playback at $863E. Without it the tick clears all three SID voice controls.
SID base offsets 0, 7 and 14 for the three voice register blocks.
Track identifier retained for a stream restart and for indexing effect data.
Length table indexed by the current track or effect selector at $8F08, used when the per-voice counter wraps.
Indexed parameter bytes changed by command $9B.
Low bytes of the three selected voice stream pointers, copied to $F0 for the active decoder.
High bytes paired with $8F13. Copied to $F1 before reading the selected event.
Per-voice flag that event $B3 sets and event $B2 clears.
Operand of event $B3, one byte per indexed voice.
Repeat counts decremented by command $94.
Low byte of the repeat target installed by command $95.
High byte of the repeat target restored when the $94 command loops.
Saved stream return field used by the command handlers.
The other byte of the saved stream return position.
Low byte of the selected pitch word set by $8AC8.
High byte of the selected pitch word set by $8AD0.
Per-voice offset reset by the event setup and incremented by the effect calculation.
The indexed pitch byte stored after adding the event's transpose field. Read again for modulation and effect playback.
Duration or position byte incremented at $891A for the enabled secondary effect.
Set by $88 and cleared by $87. The effect-age path tests this before advancing.
Enable flag checked at $8950. Commands $8E and $8D arm and clear it.
Per-voice phase reset during setup and advanced in the $896F and $8984 paths.
Signed arithmetic parameter consumed by the three add/subtract branches of the $8E modulation.
Set by command $A2 and cleared by $A0 or $A1. This gates the second modulation calculation.
Running position loaded and advanced between $89AB and $89D2.
Increment added to the evolving pitch or phase at $89D9.
Comparison value at $89B3, derived from the $A2 command parameter.
The other byte used in the comparison at $89AE.
Decremented while modulation is active. Reloaded from $8F5B when needed.
Saved delay from the first parameter of command $8E.
Per-voice delay decremented at $899E.
Initial and reset delay for the $A2 modulation countdown.
Stored waveform control for the first voice. Indexed reads at $870B and $87AE allow the common path to use this or either adjacent control byte.
Second voice control initialised from the fixed waveform defaults by $8B2D.
Third voice's waveform control initialised at $8B33.
First per-voice delay counter, reduced by $8664 until the next event is due.
Delay counter for the middle voice. Initialised to two during voice setup.
Last per-voice delay field. Initialised to three during voice setup.
Running timer for the event tick. When it expires the driver reloads it from $FF.
Voice fields set after selecting the pitch value at $86BB.
Mode bit set by $A9 and cleared by $A8.
Companion mode bit set by $A8. The modulation logic changes it while updating the effect.
Per-voice option set and cleared by $B1 and $B0, checked in the envelope path at $88C7.
Per-voice position reset by event setup and advanced by the envelope-effect routine.
Auxiliary mode flag set by $8F or $91 and cleared by $90.
Counter incremented in the $8F-mode branch at $88F9.
Copied from $8F8D on setup and updated when the effect changes the pitch.
Per-voice preset initialised from the driver defaults beginning at $914D. Command $A4 can replace it.
First per-voice operand set by $9C and read when applying the effect in the voice tick.
Second parameter set by $9C, alongside $8F90.
Cutoff accumulator changed by the running filter code before updating the SID.
Reload value for the cutoff. Initialised to the same command operand as $8F96.
Filter movement step added or subtracted by the filter tick.
Global flag used by the filter tick at $8806 and cleared by command $92.
Per-voice switch controlling which way the effect modifies cutoff within the filter step.
First operand of command $A7 and an input to the addition at $89F6.
The other byte supplied by command $A7.
Per-voice flag set and cleared by $8C and $8B.
Low byte used by the effect routines to update the pitch accumulator, with overflow carried into $8FAF.
High byte of the running effect pair. Advanced when updates to $8FAC carry or borrow.
Enable field set by $A7 and cleared by $A6.
Operand loaded by the $A8 and $A9 shared command path. The tick adds or subtracts it from the effect value.
Countdown decremented by the $A8/$A9 effect path.
Low byte of the target pitch word indexed by the transposed note and stored at $8C77. Used in the running effect comparison.
High byte of the target pitch word stored at $8C7D, restored with the low byte at $8FBB when the running effect applies the target.
State tested at $8A6A. Command $A4 enables the effect and $A3 clears it.
Parameter from command $A4, read by the alternate effect path.
Per-voice offset added to a note event before selecting its SID frequency word.
Saved low byte of the target for a $9E repeat block.
High byte of the same repeat block target.
Counter read by $9E and decremented by $9D.
Flag set by events $97 and $98 and cleared by $96.
Running step count of the option at $8FD3.
Temporary byte used by the event parser when computing the next length value.
Per-voice flag checked by the effect tick at $8858.
Voice mode set by the envelope preset command and cleared by the $89 reset command.
Per-voice effect index advanced at $87C2 before the lookup at $87EE.
Table read by the effect lookup at $87F1. The index is chosen from the running effect state.
Per-voice byte read by the preset-effect path and advanced or reset as playback progresses.
Counted by $885D and reset when it reaches the effect length indexed at $8F09.
Temporary byte holding one plus Y while advancing the bytecode pointer.
Bit masks XORed into the SID routing register by the $92 handler.
Low-address values for the selectable envelope preset read. The command uses its low three bits to index this table.
Low byte of the patched handler address selected from $9165.
High byte of the function pointer used by the indirect JMP at $86A7.
Voice index preserved across command decoding while X is used as table scratch.
Pitch-index changes read by the effect calculation at $87D1.
Packed sequences read by indexed voice effects. Their values include SID control bytes and offsets in the pitch table.
Attack and decay values selected from the low bits of the envelope preset command.
Sustain and release values paired with those at $9065.
Little-endian SID pitch words. $8AC8 doubles the pitch number and reads the two bytes into indexed voice fields.
High byte of the first little-endian pitch word. $8AD0 uses this base with the same doubled pitch index as the low-byte read.
Six fixed defaults copied to the attack-decay and sustain-release registers of the three SID voices by $8AFA-$8B1B.
Fixed voice 1 sustain-release value written to SID register $D406.
Fixed voice 2 attack-decay value written to SID register $D40C.
Fixed voice 2 sustain-release value written to SID register $D40D.
Fixed voice 3 attack-decay value written to SID register $D413.
Fixed voice 3 sustain-release value written to SID register $D414.
Fixed tempo reload value copied into $FF by $8B21.
Initial stored first voice waveform control.
Initial stored second voice waveform control.
Initial stored last voice waveform control.
Eighteen bytes copied to the state area beginning at $8F8D before the first events of the track.
Track pointer bytes used by $8ADF to initialise the three voice streams.
Little-endian handler addresses indexed by the command's low seven bits. The dispatcher at $8695 patches $9001/$9002 with the selected destination.
High-byte base one byte into the command address table. Read alongside $9165 with a doubled opcode index.
Notes and command payloads for the sound driver. For example the stream beginning at $91F2 contains $95 calls and positions in this same region. The voice reader interprets these bytes through $8678.
Save A, Y and X, acknowledge the interrupt, set the raster compare to line 255 and restore this handler's address to the hardware IRQ vector. Start CIA 2 timer A and enter the video update.
Reload the loop's self-modified immediate after composing the sprite X high-bit mask, then advance to the next hardware slot.
Immediate restored from the hardware sprite slot loop at $9455, before stepping to the next set of sprite registers.
Save A, Y and X and read CIA 2's interrupt flags. If its interrupt bit is set, disable the indicated sources and reload timer A with $FFFF before continuing.
Move all sprite X positions offscreen and switch to the HUD VIC bank, screen and charset. Wait for the split line, enable the status display and call the sound tick later in the lower border.
Continue writing the alternate sprite pointer sequence. Wait for the hardware sprite Y, flip the playfield buffer and schedule another sprite IRQ when the queue and line bounds allow it.
Set raster line 5 and redirect the hardware IRQ vector back to $9389 before restoring registers and returning.

Acknowledge the raster interrupt, find the hardware slot from $13 modulo eight, then replace its position, colour and shape. Schedule the next sprite IRQ using the next queued sprite Y, or return to the normal split.
Immediate patched with the next logical sprite number by $969F.

Fetch the queued sprite X and Y and update the corresponding VIC registers. The next instructions copy its colour and shape to both possible screen pointer tables and change only the selected X high bit.
Acknowledge the raster and CIA flags and set up a return to $9757 on line 0. Call the music driver before restoring the interrupted registers.
Schedule the other title IRQ on line 250. Update the title's border, display control and sprite positions, and populate the title screen sprite pointer table with $4C-$53.
Preserve A while reading CIA 2 interrupt status to clear its latched flags, then return from NMI.
Derive tile coordinates and the screen origin from the scroll position. Draw eight rows of ten tiles using the map pointed to by the patched operand at $98AB and the four quadrants at $0B00-$0E00.
Initial X index patched according to the half-tile position of the viewport.
Indexed tile-grid read. The operand is rewritten at $9894/$989C for the first row and then advanced by $60 per row at $9905-$9910.
Low byte of the tile map address composed from the row table and starting column.
High byte of the renderer's absolute map operand. $989C selects the first row and $9910 increments it on a page crossing.
Low byte of the initial top-left destination patched before drawing the tile row.
High byte of the target for the upper-left character, patched from the active screen's page.
Low byte of the initial top-right screen destination.
High byte of the target for the upper-right character. Its column is one character to the right of the upper-left store.
Low byte for the lower-left character target, offset one row from the upper-left.
High byte of the target for the lower-left character. The low-byte destination starts one screen row after the top-left cell.
Low operand of the fourth store, one column right of the lower-left.
High byte of the lower-right cell store patched by $9861 and advanced along with the other three target addresses after a row.
Centre the viewport on the player by subtracting $B8 horizontally and $64 vertically. Clamp the origins to $04D0 and $0790 and mask the scroll direction flags when an axis is at its limit.

Dispatch on the stage index at $FFF8. For the forest, test the scroll origin against per-row thresholds and offset coordinates through $9BFC and $9C2A. The city thresholds begin at $9A7A, which returns for stage indices 2 through 4.
Test the viewport's high and low bytes for the lower region. Select each rebase's pair of signed X and Y offsets before returning.
Continue only for stage index 1. Compare the viewport origin with city-specific seams and reposition the indexed objects through the signed X and Y offset helpers.
Page values for the two playfield buffers. The draw routine copies the selected byte into each of the four store operands.
Clear alternate camera mode and converge on the default player offset. Move the view X by eight and Y by two per pass and redraw until neither coordinate needs another step.
Immediate reload patched from the number of axes adjusted by the camera recenter step.
Add the signed word from A:X to slot 0 and slots 3 through 12 in the planar X-coordinate arrays at $0400 and $0418.
Apply the A:X offset to slots 3 through 12 and the player in the Y-coordinate arrays at $0430 and $0448.
Sort the logical sprite permutation at $C2A1 in descending screen Y. The insertion moves a sprite earlier if its Y is greater than the preceding sprite's.
Write zero to the sixteen VIC sprite coordinate bytes and their X high-bit register.

Compute a source and destination sprite address in patched operands. Copy 63 visible bytes unchanged in one facing direction, or reflect their two-bit pixels and permute the byte offsets in the other.
Patched low byte of the unchanged sprite cell source.
Patched page of the unchanged sprite copy's read.
Low byte of the bank-relative destination for the unreflected sprite.
High byte of the destination pointer for the original-facing sprite copy. It is patched together with the mirror destination at $9CED.
Low address byte of the original sprite data read in the reflection loop.
Patched source address high byte used by the reflection loop when reading the next source pixel byte.
Low byte of the destination address aligned to a 64-byte VIC sprite slot.
High byte of the destination shared by each offset in the reflected sprite layout.
Start the object's visibility test at slot $17, instead of the normal path's slot $14.

Iterate candidate objects and convert world coordinates into screen-relative offsets by subtracting the viewport and border. Reject objects beyond the horizontal or vertical limits before consulting the screen buffers.
Patched low address byte used by the screen occupancy check in the first scrolling page.
High address byte for the first scrolling-screen occupancy branch.
Low address byte of the same column in the alternate scrolling buffer.
Patched page byte for the second screen test. The routine checks the same cell offset in both buffers for overlay character codes at or above $F0.
Set the sixteen entries at $05D0 to $10 before the sprite scheduler builds the first queue.
Add the frame's vertical correction to the flagged queues and the horizontal signed correction to the X bytes of the independently flagged queues.
Copy the priority order from $C2A1, then build intermediate arrays from $0678 and $0691. Clamp one field to a minimum of $10 and copy associated colour and shape data.
Reorder locations, colour and pointer entries into the queue read by the multiplex interrupt, using $0668 as the source-index array.

Check the high bit of player state $04C0 and the remaining state bits to choose an animation branch. In the ordinary state, derive the next walking or standing frame from the active-low direction inputs and a two-pass countdown.
For object index X, add the caller's horizontal and vertical offsets in A and Y to its position. Convert the result to tile coordinates, then look up the stage tile and its property.
This immediate byte is patched to $00 or $FF at $A022 so that the horizontal sampling offset can be added as a signed value.
Read the collision cell ID through the absolute operand patched by $A083 and $A08B. The subsequent indexed read fetches that tile's property byte at $0F00.
Low byte of the map address. The tile samplers' final indexed property read uses the ID loaded through this patched operand.
High byte of the tile-map address read by the instruction at $A08E. Before the final address is formed this byte is also scratch for calculating the tile row.
Update facing from the horizontal input when the player's state permits it. Suppress the standing-fire path during the normal movement delay, and in the mode with bit 7 set mask the vertical input.

Test active-low fire. When a shot is allowed, initialise its coordinates from the player's position, set direction and timing fields and activate the slot with $8A. The no-shot path tries the attack routine at $BF47.

Interpret direction bits while the player's low state bits indicate rest. Set the airborne flag for up, the duck flag for down and the horizontal flag for left or right. Probe tiles below both sides of the player before deciding if the ground supports the sprite.
When bit 0 is set, update Y from the signed motion table at $C281/$C291. Sample the tiles below the sprite to detect a landing or the tile property that enters the climb state.

On a horizontal airborne pass, select the step size at $C246 and sample the tile next to the player. Property 3 selects the blocked path. Otherwise update X in the facing direction, preserve the resulting carry or borrow in the high byte, and advance the animation fields.
Align X to a 16-pixel column while climbing. Left or right changes the state and reinitialises motion. Up and down test property 2 before changing Y by eight.
Test the low state flags and active-low fire. The fire path sets bit 4 and continues into the following attack logic. A direction change can clear the crouch and attack flags.
The tile-query result from $A48D is overwritten by the read of the joystick latch here. This branch uses the fire bit and the low-nibble direction mask.
Align the player's Y position when the floor test resolves. The next path returns to grounded movement.
XOR bit 7 of the player's state byte at $04C0.

Probe the tile in front of the player's facing direction. Unless property 3 stops movement, change X by eight and set the corresponding direction bit. Clear the movement-state bits and test the following tile.
Use $0418/$0400 as a world X pair. Clamp it to $0020 at the left edge and $05FA at the right edge.
Constrain the player's X offset relative to the viewport stored in $03/$02. The bounds are $0020 and $0140 from the viewport origin.
If the current mode or player flags require it, clear the active entry at $0600 indexed by $04F0 and clear $04F0. Adjust one of the state counters based on bit 7 of the player flags.

In normal gameplay move the object at $0449/$0431 by eight per update, reversing when it reaches $0182 or $02E2. After moving, test two offsets for tile property 5 and set a direction-dependent flag in $29.

Clear prior overlap flags and scan the non-player entries. Skip inactive entries and mode 5. Flag overlap when the 16-bit coordinate differences fit the horizontal and object-specific vertical bounds.
Clear the encounter request and auxiliary flag, then select the encounter routine from $FFF8. In ordinary play check the current stage's positional trigger.
Require player X in $0368-$03EC and player Y exactly $016C, with the object control byte at $051D nonnegative. Then raise the encounter request at $57 and set the associated counters.
Test the first city encounter's position and its one-shot byte at $051D. The success path selects the encounter state and initialises its associated object.
Use the separate one-shot byte at $051E and the city coordinate comparison to set the third encounter state.
At Y $00FC and X $0202-$0272, check the nonnegative trigger byte at $051F. Set $57 and $63 to 4 and mark the trigger byte with $FF.
Require Y $00FC and X at least $03E6. Set the encounter flag and auxiliary value when $051C is nonnegative, then store the camera anchor and enter $A8CF.
Address byte in the initial check of the player's Y high byte at $A9CF. The trigger requires that byte to be zero.
Require Y $015C and X $0346-$03B9 with $051C nonnegative. Raise the encounter flag and create the accompanying object with stage colour and animation fields.
Require X $0480-$04FF and Y $076C. Latch the trigger at $051C and write the encounter object's coordinates relative to the player's position.
Require Y $077C and X at least $04EA. Initialise the trigger flags, use a fixed object position of $05A0 by $0763 and prepare its sprite fields.
If no encounter is selected in $63, enter the finish path at $AEB9. Otherwise dispatch by stage number at $FFF8.

Work on the first encounter slot only while $63 is 1 and $051D is active. After updating its counter, copy the position to a working slot, select its sprite animation and apply the collision routine before updating the stage display.
For encounter type 2, clear the encounter if its latch is negative. Otherwise step the object coordinates using the signed C2xx/C3xx increments and update its animation through $AE58.
Accept encounter types 1, 3 and 4. If the encounter's latch is negative, clear its flags. Otherwise apply the effect at $AF55 and count down $04A5, marking $051D and ending the encounter at zero.
Subtract the viewport from the object selected by Y. Write its low Y and both X bytes into $7D and $7A/$7B.

Test the object's low hit flags, update the collision effect, and retire a projectile from its active slot. Decrease the object's hit counter by one or by three when the player-state sign bit is set. At zero or underflow mark it defeated and clear $63.
Set the colour to 7 and activate two of the effect slots per pass. Continue updating the active entries until the counter bounds are reached.
When $63 is nonzero, scan the upper object slots for overlap flags and call $BCD8 on each hit.
Find a free projectile slot and require the noise index to reach $E2. Copy the encounter object's coords into the slot, subtract the requested Y offset and activate it with a $14 countdown.
Immediate offset set from A at $AF18, subtracted from the new projectile Y coordinate.
Subtract four from X for slot $15, including borrow into its high byte.
Subtract eight from the 16-bit X coordinate of slot $14.

Move the displayed values at $5F and $61 a step toward their targets at $68 and $69. A target of $28 or above selects a decrement. If the resulting $5F is at least $28, set the exit flag $64 and reset both $5F and $68 to $27.
Return the high nibble in A and the low nibble in Y. Both digits start in the byte passed in A.
Split the packed decimal score and timer bytes into digit nibbles. Convert the score and timer digits to character codes starting at $D2, then draw the lives display and write the associated colours.
Four character codes for the low-bit remainder of either status meter. The update uses three low bits of the meter value, divided by two, to select a cell in this table.
Set up the title IRQ, character display and logo sprites, then animate the title until port 2 fire is pressed following a release.
Signal the title IRQ through $10 and wait for it to clear that flag.
Install the title IRQ and the CIA2 acknowledgement NMI, disable multicolour mode and sprites during setup, then select the title's VIC bank, screen and font.
Read packed BCD score entries at $C465 through $C473. Extract the upper digit and add screen-code base $30 before writing the corresponding high-score display row.
Insert the current score and an empty name after the existing entries, then sort adjacent three-byte packed BCD scores in descending order and carry the eight-character names with each swap.
Select the score row. For each of eight positions blink its colour, let joystick up and down change the screen code and commit the character to the name table on fire.
Copy the eight screen codes from each saved name to its row beginning at $C832, mask the high bits and set its colour to 1 before drawing the scores.
When its counter allows it, advance through the title colour sequence. On reaching a zero entry reset the sequence and redraw the score names.
Decrement the title's initial countdown or alternate the two animation phases. Advance the upper line index on one phase and decrease the lower index on the other.
Prepare the copy source and row count for the title's upper moving stripe. Patch the destination from the active row and advance the source as the loop runs.
Low operand of the title's first stripe data read.

Low byte of the destination address for the upper stripe.

Set the lower strip's source to $C4B0 and draw thirteen rows from the current lower cursor.
Compute a screen address from the current row, copy a six-character stripe from a patched source in the title template and advance the source by six for each iteration.
Low address byte advanced by six for each lower stripe row.
High byte of the lower stripe source, updated when the low byte carries.
Patched column address for the lower strip's write.
Patched high byte of the screen cell destination for the lower title stripe.
Change the title-logo position accumulator used by the title interrupt.
Write the title's score row background values across the five displayed rows as the initial countdown ends.
Fill the four title screen pages with the current display fill character while preparing the associated colour pages.
Select a character mask and replacement bits using projectile state. Calculate the addressed cell of the active screen and combine its glyph with the mask in the character copy at $B5D0.

Patched high address of the next cell in the selected scrolling screen.
Scan the eight projectile slots. For active entries, convert their position relative to the camera into character coordinates for drawing, sample the tile properties and update or retire the slot.
Update the transient sprite animation state used during the encounter-mode renderer.
Select the animation through the type and frame indices. Patch the part record address, mirror its X offset according to facing and append part positions and sprite pointers to the queue.
Low byte of the selected animation table address supplied to the player part builder.
High-byte operand patched from $C6AB and used to select the player's animation header.
Patched pointer low byte for the colour, shape and displacement record read.
Patched high byte of the sprite part read at $B746. Consume one colour/shape/displacement record per queued part.
Iterate object slots $14 down through 3. Advance and wrap their animation counters unless bit 2 of the flags inhibits it. Dispatch the active slot according to the low flags at $0520.
Clear the sixteen per-sprite Y fields and scan object coordinates against the viewport. The routine builds screen positions and chooses slots for the objects the raster IRQ will display.
Select the animation table from the object's type and frame, carry facing and mode information into the builder and load the pointer to this frame's parts.
Low byte of the object's frame header table selected at $B951.
High-byte operand of the object's patched header read.
Low byte of the object's current sprite part record pointer.

Scan object slots and dispatch their upgrade or spawn path from the state fields. The calls at $BA28 and $BA4D use the object's state to choose the update.

For an eligible city position, use the noise index to decide whether to try the alternate spawn. Otherwise retain the current object index, sample the tile in front of the player and dispatch using the generated byte and a facing flag.
Check the stage spawn latch, read an initial coordinate pair from the C5xx tables and set the object's animation fields if its position passes the proximity check.
Inspect the player state sign bit to choose the contact effect when a non-player overlap is flagged.
Select the points increment from $C185 based on the player-state sign bit. Add with carry across the three packed BCD score bytes.
Convert eight stage-local entries from tile coordinates to pixels. Set up their object flags, shape counters and variant bytes in the per-object arrays.
Loop over slots $0C-$13, mark flagged pickups inactive, add either five or ten to the second meter target capped at $27 and award twenty points using packed decimal arithmetic.
Clear the self-modifiable scratch at $BDB6 before checking the collection flags.
Set during $BD6C if a pickup slot was marked collected.
Search the eight entries at $0600 from high to low. On a free slot return its index in Y with carry clear. If all slots are busy return carry set.
Select a 16-bit X offset from $C17F/$C180, add it to the viewport X, and use the player's Y as the new object's Y.
Look up the stage position pair in the object spawn tables, using carry to signal whether this spawn passes the position tests.
Subtract the viewport's X from the indexed object X. Return carry clear within the permitted horizontal span, with its low byte in Y.
Set the projectile Y to the source object's Y minus $20. Arm its slot and countdown with $14, then cancel it if the horizontal position falls outside the window.
Add A to the low byte of the indexed object's X coordinate. Use Y as the high offset with carry.
Use the marker index at $AB to choose the active column and patch the widths for the two adjacent strip updates.
Patched immediate subtracted from the row width $28 to choose the next strip's starting column.
Patched immediate subtracted from $0E before entering the row-address helper.
Set the two store operands to the paired screen buffers. Clear the selected column in both, then advance each pointer by a forty-byte row.
Low byte of the store in the first screen buffer, incremented by the row stride.
Page byte of the first screen column clear operation.
Low byte of the store in the alternate screen buffer.
Patched high byte of the second screen's strip store, incremented when stepping to the next row propagates carry.
Compute the screen offset using the row table and patch the row read or write in the marker path.
Low byte of the marker cell patched in the first screen.
High byte of the first screen's patched marker write.
Low byte of the marker cell in the other screen.
Patched high byte of the character write into the alternate playfield screen.

On active-low fire with no swing running, create the four-pass attack in slot 2. Select its shape from facing and invert the low shape bit when player state bit 5 is set. Copy the player position and add $10 to attack Y when state bit 2 is set. Hide the slot at expiry.

If the attack flag at $30 is set, scan active objects. Compute the signed displacement from object slot 2 and use the direction at $053A to choose the left or right rectangular test. Clear the target's field at $04F0 on a hit.
Eight table indices selected by the timer-driven movement state in $C065.
Eight scroll direction values selected by the phase in $91 at $C137.
Low signed X step for a projectile, indexed by twice its direction value.
High byte for the same signed X step, added with carry by $B699.
Column offsets loaded into the two subtract operands in the marker update.
Indexed value loaded into the spawn scratch at $45 according to the player's facing.
Low offset added to the viewport when placing a spawned object.
High offset paired with $C17F in the little-endian spawn position table.
Horizontal sample offset indexed by facing for the tile query in the duck or attack path.
BCD score increment selected by the player's state for the contact award routine.
Alternate animation type selected after the tile collision at $B85A.
Replacement movement flags selected from the current flags when an object hits property 3.
Offsets used to pick a group of twenty bytes from the forest encounter row template at $CB04.
Character codes read by $AEE6 as the exit effect fills its stage display work row.
Page values for the two active sprite-pointer tables. The raster path patches $9628 before writing the queued shape bytes.
Horizontal offsets added to the encounter object's screen X when positioning adjacent hardware sprites.
Five low bytes of the stage-specific player X coordinate. $8280 selects it using the stage value at $FFF8.
Five high bytes paired with the stage X low table at $C1C0.
Five low bytes of the starting Y position from $8286.
High bytes of the starting Y position, selected by the same stage number at $8292.
Five stage-dependent bytes used by the raster code for the playfield colour settings.
Second stage-specific multicolour choice read by the top-area raster code.
First additional stage-specific multicolour byte used at $9409.
Mutable colour value written by the final encounter path and consumed by the raster setup.
One fill byte per stage used for the four colour RAM pages upon entry.
One mask per VIC sprite slot, with that slot's bit clear. $96E9 clears the old X high bit before putting the new one in.
A single-bit value for an X high-bit update, or zero for the index group used when the slot has no high bit.
Stored values for $D018 selected by the scroll page during the raster path.
High-byte offsets selected by the active scroll page in the projectile drawing path.
Associated byte added to the projectile's cell offset.
Values mixed into $29 after adding the rightward air increment.
Values mixed into $29 after subtracting the mirrored air increment.
Horizontal increments while airborne. The player update holds at the previous entry on $FF and subtracts this magnitude when facing left.
Direction bits copied to $29 alongside the indexed vertical movement step.
Airborne animation index for the corresponding point in the vertical sequence. $A3B3 adds six to set the following boundary.
Low byte of the signed Y step added by the airborne movement code. $FF makes the index hold at the preceding entry.
High byte added with carry after the low-byte Y step at $A297.
Address one byte before the permutation used by the sort. Lets X name the previous sprite while the other read names the current one.
Sixteen indices sorted by descending screen Y by $9C58. When the selected sprite's Y becomes greater than the preceding sprite's Y, it moves earlier in the permutation.
Output positions used by the sprite reflection loop. It reads 63 input bytes in reverse loop order and uses this table to permute them when facing the opposite way.
Low byte of the signed object X increment, indexed by the encounter movement phase.
High byte of the object X increment. Added with carry from the low coordinate byte.
Low byte of the first encounter object's vertical increment, indexed alongside its X increment.
High byte paired with the vertical step at $C312.
Low byte used for the Y motion of the object in slot $14 during the shared encounter path.
High byte of the signed Y motion paired with $C332.
Low bytes of screen row offsets added to the template base by $B46C and several routines with patched screen reads.
High bytes of the row offsets, combined with the carry from the low-byte screen calculation.
Relative indices for the scan of both scrolling screens at $9D94, while checking characters against the $F0 threshold.
Low bytes of the initial shot's horizontal offset indexed by facing. $A1CE adds the selected value to the shot X.
High bytes of the same facing-dependent shot offset, applied with carry at $A1D7.
One group of projectile offsets indexed by the noise-based enemy spawn branch.
Companion offsets read by the same branch at $BAE7.
Selection table for horizontal scroll control in the first pending phase in the lower-area interrupt.
Horizontal scroll control for the second step, which also flips the screen-buffer selector at $08.
Low-byte X corrections associated with the pending scroll flags. The interrupt sign-extends the chosen byte into $33.
Value copied into $07 for the first display shift step during the lower-area interrupt.
Value copied into $07 for the second step of the shift.
Logical sprite Y corrections selected using the pending scroll flags. The interrupt applies the value through $32.
Eight screen codes for the first high-score name.
Eight screen codes for the second high-score name.
Eight screen codes for the third high-score name.
Eight screen codes for the fourth high-score name.
Eight screen codes for the fifth high-score name.
Eight spaces put in place before entering a new name after the score is ranked.
First byte of each three-byte packed BCD entry, used for the leading decimal pair and compared before the other two bytes when ranking.
Middle byte of each packed BCD entry. When the leading bytes tie, the rank comparison at $B2C9 uses this byte.
Final byte of a score. $B2D5 compares it when the first two bytes tie.
Address of the next entry's leading byte relative to the ranking index from $B2BD, also read to draw the second score line.
Leading tie-break byte of the second record read by $B2C9.
Last tie-break byte of the second record read by $B2D5.
Offset of the third saved score in the table, read when drawing the third line.
Offset of the fourth saved score in the table, read when drawing the fourth line.
Offset of the fifth saved score in the table, read when drawing the fifth line.
Leading packed decimal byte of the candidate score, copied from $87 by $B2A3.

AND masks for the projectile character compositing path, selected at $B5D3.
OR values paired with the projectile glyph masks, read at $B5D6.
Eight-character name-table offset for the selected score row, passing through X at $B33F.
Display column offset for name editing, loaded into Y at $B33C.
Byte sequence copied to the title colour at $97. The zero entry resets the cycle cursor and ends the transition.
Two bytes read by the title IRQ at $978A to alternate VIC control register $D011.
Six-character rows used by the title scroll copy. The routine advances the source by six and patches its destination to the current screen row.
Default operand observed at $B4C6 in the play snapshot. Later title passes patch this operand to other six-byte rows within the character template.
Packed little-endian X positions. The spawn routine at $BC8D copies the low byte into the object's X array.
High bytes interleaved with the X lows. $BC93 takes the high byte with the same offset Y.
Packed Y coordinate words paired with the X positions, read by $BC99.
High-byte base for the initial object Y, read by $BC9F.
Eight initial X coordinates by section, in 16-pixel units. $BD0D indexes the section times eight and shifts each value left by four.
Initial Y coordinates in 16-pixel units, expanded into the two Y bytes alongside the X values.
Low bytes of the source addresses used when preparing the alternate player's first sprite cell.
High bytes interleaved with the low source bytes.
Low byte of the second source passed to $9CA5 for the alternate player shape.
High byte paired with $C5DE for the second generated sprite.

High byte of the third source address.
Interleaved fields for the ordinary player animation lookup at $9E9D and $9EA0.

Header area containing the frame tables selected by $B951 and $B957. For each frame the routine reads four bytes and uses the resulting pointer at $B981.
This page has loaded animation data in the hand-over. The title clears it temporarily for VIC screen use. The engine moves all four pages to $0400 before the title and restores them afterwards.
Default screen-cell destination for the lower six-character strip. In play this address is part of the animation storage.
Destination of the first displayed high-score name, temporarily using the resident animation buffer.
First score row's leading digit cell, written by the high-nibble path.

First of the third record's score cells.

Pointer $4C, set at $9799 for the S shape.

Add $3B to the requested selection to choose the initial byte of the two-character filename at $CC20. Set up device 8, pass that filename to SETNAM and call the stream loader before restarting at $8000.
Two PETSCII bytes passed to SETNAM at $CC14. The first is generated from the selection and the second is the filename wildcard.
Open the selected file on device 8, talk on its secondary address and receive its stream via the KERNAL serial bus routines. Close the channel and clear serial I/O state after the transfer.
Fetch five bytes from the serial stream into $FB through $FF. Enter the unpacker when the serial status has not reached end-of-file.
Hide the I/O page while unpacking and allow the decoder to read the next stream byte through $CD93, which temporarily changes the processor port to restore chip access.
Decode the next token of the stage byte stream. Literal runs read bytes from the serial stream and match runs copy at an offset from the descending destination pointer in $FC/$FD.
Shift the zero-page bit reservoir $FB. Refill from the stream when its sentinel reaches carry.
Select serial bytes for a literal token, or use the backward match pointer. Decrement the output pointer before writing the run to RAM.
Use the decoded low-byte run length to move the descending destination pointer and emit the bytes of the current match or literal run.
The next immediate byte is altered by the caller to choose the serial byte path or the back-reference byte.
Self-modified immediate whose zero setting reads the disk stream and whose nonzero setting loads from the back-reference pointer in $F7/$F8.
Change the processor port for the serial bus, fetch the next byte through $EE13 and restore the port before returning.
Count of distance bits to consume for each match form in $CCE7-$CCF7.
Title character codes $00-$5F in the charset selected with VIC bank $C000 and $D018 = $24. The letter codes are $01-$1A and decimal digits are $30-$39.

Sprite pointers $4C-$53 select these eight 64-byte cells. The title snapshot places them in ascending order in the pointer table at $CBF8. The rendered cells contain the seven STRIDER letters and a blank last cell.
Twelve 64-byte slots from sprite index $54 through $5F in bank $C000. Every pixel byte is zero and the trailing bytes retain a nonzero value. The meaning of those trailing values is open.
Character indices $00-$7F of the HUD charset. The raster split selects this bank-relative character address by writing $A6 to $D018 after switching to bank $C000.
Character indices $80-$FF of the HUD charset. Rendered digits occupy $D2-$DB. Each digit takes eight raster bytes and the font ends with empty entries.

Eight-byte graphic cells in the $E000 page. In the rendered cells $04, $06 and $08 carry repeating vertical strips, while $01-$03 form layered horizontal bands. The same bytes are present in the alternate release.
Graphic cells $10-$22 include another group of multicolour strips and the narrow tapered elements seen at $16-$1A. The route selecting these cells remains open.
First page of the authored HUD screen-code template. $84FF copies it to $EA58 and looks up colors by glyph at $E800.
Second page of the template, copied to $EB00 by $850C. The two destination pages overlap where the second begins.
Rendered bitmap glyphs starting with A through Z, then digits and punctuation. Each takes eight bytes, starting at offset $0500 from $E000. The display path selecting this group remains open.

Twelve eight-byte glyphs. The first three have a blank leading row above seven repeated colour rows. The block then progresses from blank to a full rectangle and down through the stepped edge masks to a single filled row.
Eight rows of $20, rendering a narrow vertical column in the last cell of the upper glyph page.
Foreground colour indexed by a HUD screen code. The draw routine reads it before the stores to colour RAM at $8509 and $8516.
Sixteen 64-byte sprite cells in bank $C000, indexes $B0-$BF. The rendered group starts with patterned fragments and transitions into angular lines and figure forms.
Sixteen sprite records with isolated humanoid and diagonal pose shapes along the first row of the upper-bank asset render.
Upper-bank sprite cells $D0-$DF. The render includes long narrow lines and separate mechanical fragments.
Upper-bank sprite cells $E0-$EF, showing paired tall shapes and long curved forms.
Four upper-bank sprite records with repeated segment shapes. These end before the CPU-generated reflection table at $FD00.
Lookup built for indices $01-$FF at $802B-$803F by reversing the order of the four two-bit pixel pairs. Entry $00 is already zero in the snapshot and the loop leaves it unchanged.
Low bytes of the 128 multiples of $60 generated by $804A-$8062. The drawing and collision paths add a column to this base offset.
High-byte companion to $FE00. Drawing adds $10 to select the map starting at $1000.
This initial cell in VIC bank $C000 has zero pixel bytes. It is also the initial source operand of the self-modifying copy at $9CD6.
Stage index copied from the entry instruction's operand at $8001. The following hardware vector bytes at $FFFA and $FFFE are installed by the engine for NMI and IRQ.
